> The other side of that coin is detecting poor acting and lying. Challenging someone's statement. **Cockroach Poker** is one of the purest forms of this. Games like **Skull**. 

It's funny you mention those games. They're definitely not social deduction game in the sense that we usually intend but they share a common element: lying or bluffing. Both games fit neatly in the bluffing category of games but in slightly different manner: In Cockroach Poker, player need to actually lie if they want to bluff. In Skull, you never explicitly lie, you imply a lie.

This made me think what was the difference between a bluffing game and a social deduction game. Both genres have players deceive their fellow players, and both genres have players call or deduce the elements of deceptions. I think the fundamental difference in both kinds of games is in the origin of the lie. In a social deduction game, the players are usually set aside in two groups: the deceivers and the detectives. The origin of the lie comes from the unchanging identity of those players. In a typical bluffing game, the roles of deceivers and detectives are either one and the same, or constantly changing.

You also speak of the purest form of such games, and I believe that both bluffing games and social deduction games have the same game as their purest form: **Win, Lose or Banana.**

There are two main paths that depend on a combination of two resources. You should have an idea of which direction you’re going as you place your first settlements

The first path is gathering Wood/Brick to build lots of settlements and roads. You’ll win the game if you can get the longest road and spread out settlements.

The second path is gathering Ore/Wheat to build lots of cities and buy development cards. I prefer this route, but it may be less powerful with regular players. You need fewer settlements and space as you get most of your points from largest army or development cards

Returning to initial placement, the dots below each number represent their frequency. If you add the dots surrounding one spot you can easily compare resource flow to other spots. Take a look at the board and notice if any resources are especially scarce. You could try to corner the market for this.

Hope this helps!
